text:
I’ve been using the DGX Spark a lot lately, mainly running either the Qwen 3.8 27B + Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B combination or Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, mostly via the Pi coding agent.

For the past month, I’ve also used Grok Bot in parallel. Inspired by it, I’ve integrated Grok Bot, Kimi, and the DGX into a loose workflow, using Notion, GitHub, and my PC as hubs to pass tasks between them. I haven’t pursued full-scale automation or connected things to Telegram for remote commands, since I generally use the DGX for sensitive personal or professional work.

However, my Grok Bot usage quota has drained too quickly—nearly exhausted from just casual chatting and information gathering. With the shared pool becoming a bottleneck, I installed the Hermes Agent Desktop on my PC to offload some work. It supports Grok OAuth, so I can still use it when needed, though it doesn’t support Kimi OAuth.

Then another issue arose. Work has been quite busy lately, and I’m relying more on local compute than cloud services. Grok alone is no longer sufficient; it’s fine for quick lookups, but for analyzing documents or drafting content, I have to rely on local resources. This means the DGX is almost permanently occupied by Nemotron, making it time-consuming whenever I need to switch models.

I’ve been tempted to buy another DGX—one dedicated to Nemotron, the other to Qwen. It would even allow experimenting with TP2 configurations for various MiaAI setups. But the price is significant, and while getting the first one was already incredible luck, a second one will be a major hurdle to get past my wife. After all, it’s not exactly a Hermès I’d be buying for her! I suppose I’d better stay rational.

大佬的教程特别详细，实测我就用了一句话解决，直接把你的订阅链接给muse，然后告诉他选哪条节点就好了，如果怕你的ai看不懂可以把这指令复制粘贴给他：

用我给你的订阅链接：xxxxxx帮我把你出网的默认出口换成一个固定、干净的出口，别再让你的公共池 IP 连累我的号被封。
先体检你现在的默认出口：连测 10 次出口 IP，数一数换了几个、都在哪些城市、是机房还是住宅，再用 https://t.co/guPrsCAttm查一下风控值和共享人数，结果报我。
然后逐个实测我订阅里的节点，优先选原生住宅 IP、独享或者共享人数少、风控值低、连接稳定的一个，定为固定出口，并守住这几条纪律：
1 固定出口硬连这个节点，不许自动切换、不许 fallback，不通就报错，绝不许偷偷换 IP
2 默认选择钉死它，重启也不许漂到别的国家去
3 配置只存本地一个文件，权限 600，订阅和密钥不许写进聊天和记忆
4 做成常驻服务，崩溃自己拉起来，机器重启能自恢复，再加个定时巡检，出口 IP 一变马上报我

text:
Building with Grok Bot: 

I don't own a VR headset yet. So this morning Grok Bot built me a VR world editor in Rust that I can use with a mouse and keyboard. 🦀🥽

Unreal 5.8 has its VR Template, and Meta has its Interaction SDK. I wanted the same idea in my own engine, so I can build VR training worlds now and play them when I buy a Quest.

What we built before breakfast, in about an hour and a half:

🛠️ A full desktop editor (Bevy + egui) with Outliner, Details panel, Content Browser, a move/rotate/scale gizmo with snapping, undo/redo, and save/load
📄 One scene format (RON) shared by the editor and the game, so what I build is exactly what I play
📦 Real 3D models. You drag glTF/GLB files from the Content Browser and they land on whatever surface is under the mouse
✋ VR interactions: grab and throw with physics, snap points, a wall button, a lever, teleport and no-teleport zones, trigger volumes, and a spectator camera
▶️ Play mode in the same window. Ctrl+P plays the scene with simulated VR hands, and Esc puts everything back
🎓 A Training tab where you build lessons step by step. Each step gets an instruction, what counts as done (grab, snap, button, lever, zone), hints, points and an optional time limit

The first lesson, "Workshop basics": pick up the wrench, put it on the snap point, press the red button, pull the yellow lever. A floating panel tracks your steps and score.

It wasn't all smooth. The packaged .exe crashed the moment the side panels drew. Grok Bot read the Windows crash logs, found two parts of the UI code fighting over the same data, fixed it, and added a test so it can't come back. It also added a crash log file for the future.

Then it put my TT logo on the app icon, the taskbar and the Desktop shortcut.

39 tests passing. Everything is in Rust, and Grok Bot wrote all of it. I just said what I wanted.

Next up is a second lesson, plus sound and controller buzz. And one day, an actual headset. 😄

text:
I just reduced Grok Bot's token usage by 40.6% on the same task by changing how I instructed it.

Instead of telling it what to do, I taught it how to do it.

I wanted to experiment with two different ways of getting Grok Bot to complete the exact same job.

The task was simple:

Go online and find an iPhone Duo in Night Sky with 256GB storage. Check whether it's available for delivery to Sydney, postcode 2000, and report the delivery date or whether it's out of stock.

TEST 1 - TELL GROK BOT WHAT TO DO

I gave Grok Bot the instructions and let it go online, navigate the website, find the product and check delivery availability.

Total usage: 1,316,200 tokens.

TEST 2 - TEACH GROK BOT HOW TO DO IT

This time, I took a different approach.

I used Grok Bot's computer and demonstrated the process myself while recording the screen.

I showed it where to navigate, what to click, how to find the product and where to check the delivery information.

Then I had Grok Bot watch the recording and create a reusable skill based on what I'd demonstrated.

Once the skill was ready, I gave Grok Bot the same task again, this time using the skill.

Total usage for that execution: 782,200 tokens.

THE RESULT

1 - Instructions only: 1,316,200 tokens.

2 - Using the taught skill: 782,200 tokens.

That's 534,000 fewer tokens, a 40.6% reduction on the skill-based execution.

This was one experiment, not a guarantee that every skill will deliver the same saving. Creating the skill also involved upfront work and usage.

But it demonstrates something worth investigating.

When you simply tell Grok Bot what to do, it may need to figure out how to navigate and complete the process.

When you demonstrate the process and turn it into a skill, you're giving it a reusable method to follow.

HERE'S HOW TO EXPERIMENT WITH THIS YOURSELF

1 - Choose a repeatable task Grok Bot normally completes online.

2 - Run it using ordinary instructions and record the token usage.

3 - Open Grok Bot's computer and record yourself demonstrating the process.

4 - Ask Grok Bot to review the recording and create a reusable skill that follows the demonstrated workflow.

5 - Run the same task using the skill. Compare the result, accuracy and token usage.

For a fair comparison, use the same inputs and check that both approaches produce the correct result.

MY BIGGEST TAKEAWAY

We're used to thinking of AI agents as something we give instructions to.

But for repeatable jobs, it may be worth teaching them the process once and letting them reuse it.

The real opportunity is finding which tasks benefit enough from that approach to justify the upfront effort.

text:
@bot 反馈一个 Windows 桌面端的自动更新 bug，前后折腾了我半个多小时，记录一下现象、原因和解决办法，希望官方能修。

📧 这份完整报告我已经用英文邮件发给官方支持（support@x.ai）了，这里同步公开一份，方便遇到同样问题的 Windows 用户自救。

【环境】Windows 台式机，Grok Bot 用「所有用户」方式安装（/allusers），装在自定义的 D 盘目录，不是默认路径。

【现象】
1. Grok Bot 0.78.4 在空闲时自动更新到 0.79.4，界面一直停在「Updating Grok Bot」，进度卡在 12% 不动。
2. 每次重新打开，它又重新下载安装包，就这样无限循环，临时目录里攒了好几个更新包，占了大约 500MB。
3. 手动运行新安装包，报错「Failed to uninstall old application files. Please try running the installer again.: 2」，点重试又提示「Grok Bot 无法关闭」，反复重试结果都一样。
4. 版本号始终停在 0.78.4，更新一直没成功。

【原因】
1. 新安装包会先调用旧版的卸载程序，可这时 Grok Bot 还开着，更新页还写着 agents keep running。
2. Grok Bot 和它启动的子进程一直占着安装目录里的文件，关掉后还会被自动重新拉起，所以旧卸载程序删不掉文件，返回错误 2。
3. 自动更新是静默安装，失败了没有任何提示，下次启动又重新下载，于是一直循环。

【解决办法】
1. 先备份，再删除注册表 Uninstall 下 Grok Bot 的那一项，让新安装包不再去调用旧卸载程序。
2. 把旧安装目录改个名，腾出原来的路径。
3. 在安装过程中持续结束所有 Grok Bot 进程，防止它被重新拉起后又占住文件。
4. 用 /S /allusers /D=原路径 静默安装新包，装好就是 0.79.4，不需要重启电脑。
5. 确认能正常启动后，再删掉改名的旧目录和临时目录里的旧更新包。
另外提醒一下：如果手动改 settings.json，一定要存成不带 BOM 的 UTF-8，否则客户端会报「durable file damaged」。

【建议】
1. 更新前先确认所有 Grok Bot 进程和子进程都已经退出，再开始安装。
2. 安装失败时要明确提示原因，不要静默失败、反复重新下载。
3. 能否在更新失败后自动清理多余的更新包。
